question: When a duplicate adapter row has a malformed outer key or intent_token but an intact nested adapter identity, can it be rejected as identity_unavailable while the original receipt still exposes paired timing?
hypothesis: An unusable outer key/token must not prevent the intact nested owner/actuation/key/token fingerprint from tainting the valid receipt group.
treatment: Replay the retained A01 pair with duplicate DOWN rows whose outer intent_token or key is null or a list. Compare exact frozen baseline and candidate projector and rerun duplicate, unknown-event, legacy-transition, A06 token-conflict, and A07 split-group regressions.
decision_rule: Baseline must retain a falsely paired original receipt in all four malformed cases. Candidate must return identity_unavailable plus one incomplete receipt with both intervals null for each, and pass all six targeted methods.
uncertainty: Deterministic projector tests against one retained synthetic adapter trace only; no live-control or task-effect conclusion.
